name: Tsugami Corporation
summary: Tsugami designs and manufactures precision machine tools — automatic lathes (the core), machining centers and grinding machines — plus related services. Customers are in automotive (fuel injection, drivetrain), semiconductor equipment, medical devices and general precision parts.

name: Sony Group Corporation
summary: Sony is a collection of leadership franchises. Image sensors (IMX) are a genuine technology moat: stacked CMOS, global shutter, automotive-grade qualification, and a customer list that includes every major smartphone OEM. Music owns publishing and recorded catalogs (a royalty annuity with pricing power). Games has the PS5 platform, digital store economics and IP (God of War, Spider-Man, The Last of Us). Pictures/Crun

name: Aeva Technologies, Inc.
summary: Aeva designs FMCW 4D lidar — sensors measuring velocity per point as well as range — on a silicon-photonics "lidar-on-chip" (CoreVision) plus a custom SoC (Aeva X1) (FACT, 10-K).

name: Argan, Inc.
summary: Argan's main subsidiary, Gemma Power Systems, provides engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) for gas-fired power plants, LNG terminals and industrial projects. Other subsidiaries provide telecom infrastructure and consulting.

name: Ambarella, Inc.
summary: Ambarella designs fabless, low-power AI systems-on-chip (SoCs) and the software stack that runs on them. The chip integrates the image signal processor, the CVflow neural-network accelerator, CPUs, video encoder and system functions on one die — the architectural bet being that at the edge, unlike in the data centre, "everything on one chip" beats "a collection of discrete parts" on power, latency and cost (Citi TMT

name: Amazon.com, Inc.
summary: Amazon has three engines: North America retail (e-commerce, advertising, logistics), International retail and AWS (cloud infrastructure, database, AI services). Advertising is the highest-margin piece and is growing >20%; AWS is the profit pool (~60% of operating income).

name: AppLovin Corporation
summary: AppLovin's core is AXON, a machine-learning ad-recommendation engine that matches advertisers to mobile inventory. It earns a take rate on ad spend, plus software-platform fees. The economic magic is that AXON's models improve with data density: more spend → better predictions → higher return on ad spend → more spend. That flywheel produced 55% growth at 78% operating margins.

name: Broadcom Inc.
summary: Broadcom sells semiconductors (custom ASICs, networking, wireless, broadband, storage) and infrastructure software (VMware, CA, Symantec enterprise). The moat is design-win lock-in: custom AI chips are co-designed with hyperscalers over years, and networking silicon is the industry standard. VMware has high switching costs.

name: BigBear.ai Holdings, Inc.
summary: BigBear.ai sells applied AI and analytics to the US national-security apparatus, delivered as people-plus-software on government contracts. One reporting segment; the useful decomposition is by capability [2][8]:

name: Booking Holdings Inc.
summary: Booking earns a commission (roughly 15-20% of gross booking value) from hotels and other accommodation providers. Its moat is demand aggregation: 30M+ listings, brand, loyalty (Genius), and the largest paid-search budget in travel. Hotels value the incremental demand; travellers value selection and price transparency.

name: BlackSky Technology Inc.
summary: BlackSky owns a small-satellite constellation plus a tasking/analytics platform (Spectra) and sells three things out of that stack (FY2025 10-K):

name: CarGurus, Inc.
summary: CarGurus operates a car-shopping marketplace: consumers search listings, dealers pay for leads/subscriptions, and manufacturers pay for advertising. Revenue is mostly US dealer subscriptions (~70%), with international and product revenue (CarOffer, financing) making up the rest.

name: CEVA, Inc.
summary: CEVA licenses silicon and software IP that other companies embed in their own chips. It sells no chips. Three layers, which are also the revenue disclosure:

name: Cognex Corporation
summary: Cognex sells industrial machine vision: cameras, lenses and lighting, embedded vision systems, and the software that converts pixels into a pass/fail, a measurement or a robot coordinate. Management sizes its served market at ~$7B growing 10–11% through the cycle (Baird, 10 Nov 2026 — company estimate).

name: Celestica Inc.
summary: Celestica provides design, manufacturing and supply-chain services to OEMs and hyperscalers: networking switches, servers, storage, aerospace/defense electronics and industrial hardware. The AI networking business (800G/1.6T switches) is the growth engine.

name: Edenred SA
summary: Edenred issues and manages prepaid benefit and mobility solutions: meal vouchers, fuel/fleet cards, gift cards and corporate payments. Revenue comes from issuer fees, merchant commissions and float income. The model is a two-sided network: employers distribute benefits, employees spend them at affiliated merchants.

name: Comfort Systems USA
summary: FIX operates through regional mechanical/electrical contractors (Comfort Systems, Walker, MMC, etc.), executing design-build and installation work. The model is low-capital-intensity: customers fund projects, FIX is paid progress billing, and working capital is a source of cash when backlogs grow.

name: Alphabet Inc.
summary: Alphabet is three businesses: Google Services (Search, YouTube, Maps, Play, subscriptions), Google Cloud (GCP, Workspace, TPU/AI infrastructure) and Other Bets (Waymo, Verily, etc.). Advertising is still ~75% of revenue; Cloud is the growth and margin engine.

name: IES Holdings, Inc.
summary: IES Holdings operates through regional electrical/mechanical contractors (IES Commercial, IES Residential, IES Communications). It designs and installs electrical systems, data/communications infrastructure, HVAC and plumbing for data centers, warehouses, hospitals, schools and homes.

name: indie Semiconductor, Inc.
summary: indie designs mixed-signal SoCs and system solutions for automotive perception — radar, vision, LiDAR, ultrasound — plus in-cabin user-experience silicon and, since TeraXion/Exalos, photonics. Fabless except photonics assembly in Quebec and Switzerland; ~800 employees; 360+ issued patents (FY2025 10-K).

name: Innodata Inc.
summary: Innodata is a data engineering services company re-positioned around generative AI. Four capability blocks [3]:

name: Intuit Inc.
summary: Intuit monetises recurring compliance and financial workflows. QuickBooks is the system of record for millions of small businesses (subscription + payments + payroll + lending); TurboTax is the consumer tax franchise (unit sales plus paid upgrades); Credit Karma is an advertising/marketplace business; Mailchimp is SMB email/automation.

name: IonQ, Inc.
summary: IonQ builds trapped-ion quantum computers and sells systems, cloud access and services. It has a differentiated modality (trapped ions have high gate fidelity and all-to-all connectivity) and a growing patent portfolio. The 2025-26 acquisition spree bought photonics, networking and quantum-safe cryptography assets — a bet on becoming a full-stack quantum platform.

name: LifeMD, Inc.
summary: At the 13 Nov 2026 close of $2.195, a $5.50 average on 250 shares is about 60% under water — $549 left of $1,375 — and the stock needs a gain of roughly 151% just to get back to break-even (MarketScreener).

name: Lattice Semiconductor Corporation
summary: Lattice sells low-power, small-form-factor programmable logic and, since July 2026, platform firmware. The pitch is not raw compute — it is instant-on, deterministic, sub-watt control and connectivity next to sensors, actuators and main processors.

name: Mobileye Global Inc.
summary: Mobileye sells perception and driving-decision systems for vehicles, delivered as a tightly coupled stack of purpose-built silicon (EyeQ SoC), software (perception, REM mapping, RSS driving policy) and, increasingly, full ECUs/systems.

name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
summary: Meta sells advertising across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger and Threads. Revenue is ~98% advertising; Reality Labs (VR/AR) is a loss-making option. The moat is the largest social graph and the most sophisticated ad-targeting/measurement engine outside Google, plus 3B+ daily users.

name: Microsoft Corporation
summary: Microsoft sells productivity software (Microsoft 365, Teams), cloud infrastructure (Azure), developer tools (GitHub), gaming (Xbox/Activision), LinkedIn and Windows. The moat is enterprise switching costs, the Windows/Office standard, and Azure's hybrid-cloud footprint. AI is being layered across all of it (Copilot, Azure OpenAI, Fabric).

name: Micron Technology, Inc.
summary: Micron sells DRAM, NAND and HBM memory to data-center, mobile, PC and automotive customers. The moat is technology/manufacturing scale in a consolidated oligopoly (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron). Memory is a commodity with cyclical pricing, but HBM is more differentiated (custom packaging, qualification with Nvidia/AMD).

name: Netflix, Inc.
summary: Netflix is the largest subscription streaming service (~300M+ paid households) with a growing advertising tier. Revenue comes from subscriptions (price × members) and advertising. The moat is content scale, recommendation data and global distribution; the risk is competition (Disney+, Amazon, YouTube) and the maturity of the pay-TV replacement cycle.

name: NVIDIA Corporation
summary: Nvidia designs GPUs, networking and AI systems (DGX/HGX) and the CUDA software stack. Revenue comes from data-center AI (the vast majority), gaming, professional visualization and automotive. The moat is the CUDA ecosystem, the cadence of new architectures, and the systems-level integration (GPU+NVLink+networking+software).

name: NXP Semiconductors N.V.
summary: NXP is a broad-line semiconductor company selling microcontrollers, application processors, communication processors, connectivity chipsets, analog/interface devices, RF power transistors and security controllers, plus a growing layer of system middleware and software (FY2025 10-K, filed 19 Feb 2026).

name: Oklo Inc.
summary: Oklo designs small fast reactors (liquid-metal-cooled) and plans to own/operate them, selling electricity under long-term contracts. It also intends to build a fuel-recycling capability (using DOE material) — a potential cost advantage and a political lightning rod.

name: onsemi
summary: onsemi sells power semiconductors and sensing silicon — components, not systems or software. Three reportable segments (Q3 FY2026, 10-Q):

name: Ouster, Inc.
summary: Ouster sells sensing and perception hardware plus software to machines that need to see. Four product families:

name: Qualcomm Incorporated
summary: Qualcomm sells semiconductor platforms and patent licences. FY2026 revenue split: equipment and services $36,895M (86%), licensing $6,225M (14%) (10-K).

name: Quantinuum Inc.
summary: Quantinuum sells quantum computing hardware (H-series trapped-ion systems), cloud access, and software (TKET compiler, InQuanto chemistry, Quantum Origin cryptographic keys). Customers are governments, research labs, banks and industrials. Honeywell's backing gives it engineering discipline and a balance sheet.

name: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals
summary: Regeneron discovers and commercialises biologics. Revenue comes from Dupixent (atopic dermatitis, asthma, COPD, eosinophilic oesophagitis — shared economics with Sanofi), EYLEA/EYLEA HD (AMD, diabetic retinopathy), Libtayo (oncology), Praluent/Kevzara (legacy) and a growing oncology/immunology pipeline. It also has a large manufacturing footprint and a productive R&D engine (VelocImmune mouse platform).

name: Sanofi SA
summary: Sanofi is a global pharma with three growth engines: Immunology (Dupixent, the largest), Vaccines (flu, Beyfortus RSV, meningitis) and Oncology/rare disease (Sarclisa, Cablivi, plus acquired assets). It also has a Consumer Healthcare carve-out in progress and a legacy diabetes/ cardiovascular portfolio in decline.

name: NuScale Power Corporation
summary: NuScale designs the NuScale Power Module (77 MWe light-water SMR), the first design to receive NRC certification. Revenue comes from engineering services, licensing and project development; the long-term model is selling modules and providing fuel/services through ENTRA1, its commercialization partner.

name: Sterling Infrastructure, Inc.
summary: Sterling provides site preparation, earthwork, foundations, paving and infrastructure construction. Its e-infrastructure segment builds the civil works for data centers and semiconductor fabs — a scarce capability with high barriers (permits, equipment, skilled labour).

name: Vishay Precision Group, Inc.
summary: VPG makes precision measurement and sensing components and systems: Bulk Metal® foil resistors, foil strain gauges, load cells and force transducers, onboard vehicle-weighing systems, and specialised measurement systems for steel mills, materials research and crash testing. It was spun out of Vishay Intertechnology on 6 July 2010; the foil technology dates to Felix Zandman's work in the early 1960s (FY2025 10-K, Item

name: Vertiv Holdings
summary: Vertiv sells the plumbing and electrical backbone of data centers: UPS, power distribution, busway, thermal management (including liquid cooling), racks and monitoring software, plus a global service network. Customers are hyperscalers, colocation providers (Equinix, Digital Realty) and enterprises.

name: X-Energy, Inc.
summary: X-energy designs small modular high-temperature gas-cooled reactors (Xe-100) and manufactures TRISO fuel through TRISO-X. Revenue today comes from fuel sales, engineering services and government contracts; the long-term model is selling reactors and/or fuel to industrial customers (Dow, Amazon) and utilities.
